anomalies.observed: U4 (AVR-ISP-6) has MISO (pin1) on net PWM, SCK (pin3) on net SCK, and MOSI (pin4) on net SDA. The MCU ISP pins are not connected: U2 ATtiny45 MISO is pin6 (PWM), SCK is pin7 (POT), MOSI is pin5 (TX); U3 ATtiny13 MISO is pin6 (SCK), SCK is pin7 (POT), MOSI is pin2 (TACH).
anomalies.expected: ISP header should connect to the programming pins of the populated MCU: MISO to MISO, SCK to SCK, MOSI to MOSI, RST to RESET. For U2: U4.1->U2.6, U4.3->U2.7, U4.4->U2.5. For U3: U4.1->U3.6, U4.3->U3.7, U4.4->U3.2.

evidence.quote: U4 AVR-ISP-6: pin1 MISO -> PWM; pin3 SCK -> SCK; pin4 MOSI -> SDA. U2 ATtiny45: pin6 PWM, pin7 POT, pin5 TX. U3 ATtiny13: pin6 SCK, pin7 POT, pin2 TACH.

anomalies.impact: The board cannot be programmed via the ISP header after assembly, because the programming signals are not connected to the MCU's ISP pins.

anomalies.observed: J1 is labeled I2C and has SDA (pin1) and SCL (pin2). SDA is only connected to U4 MOSI (ISP header) and not to any MCU. SCL is not connected to any other net. U2 (ATtiny45) has USI pins PB0 (pin5) and PB2 (pin7) that should be SDA/SCL, but they are labeled TX and POT.
anomalies.expected: J1 SDA should connect to U2 pin5 (PB0/SDA) and J1 SCL should connect to U2 pin7 (PB2/SCL) for I2C operation.

evidence.quote: J1 I2C: pin1 SDA, pin2 SCL. U2 ATtiny45: pin5 TX, pin7 POT.

anomalies.impact: The I2C interface is unusable; the controller cannot communicate over I2C.

anomalies.observed: R6 10K pull-up connects the RST net to VCC (3.3V).
anomalies.expected: RST pull-up should connect to the MCU supply rail, which is +5V for both U2 and U3.

evidence.quote: R6 10K between VCC and RST. U2 VCC pin8 connected to +5V. U3 VCC pin8 connected to +5V.

anomalies.impact: The reset line may not be pulled high enough for the 5V MCUs, potentially causing unreliable reset or programming.

parsed.summary: The schematic contains several wiring errors: the ISP programming header is connected to the wrong nets, the I2C connector is not connected to the MCU, and the reset pull-up uses 3.3V instead of 5V. These would prevent programming and I2C communication.
